2609.25921.title: Toward Responsible AI-Augmented Cyber Defense: Pattern Recognition, Defense-in-Depth, and the Case for Human-AI Collaboration
2609.25921.paper_summary: Cybersecurity literature has extensively documented the operational benefits of artificial intelligence (AI) for threat detection, incident response, and prevention, while raising qualitative concerns about over-automation, algorithmic bias, and analyst-skill erosion. What remains largely absent is a formal, falsifiable model connecting three constructs that recur across this literature: Defense-in-Depth Theory, the Artificial Intelligence Theory of Pattern Recognition, and human-AI collaboration in security operations. This paper develops such a model. We formalize layered defense as a Bernoulli detection cascade in which AI augmentation enters multiplicatively across layers; we formalize each layer's pattern-recognition behavior as a Neyman-Pearson/Bayesian detector with a derived closed-form optimal threshold; and we formalize human-AI triage as a capacity-constrained cascade with an explicit, quantifiable trade-off between detection probability and false-alarm ("alert fatigue") rate. A Monte Carlo/analytical simulation evaluated at illustrative but realistic operating points shows that (i) AI augmentation compounds across defense layers, delivering its largest marginal gains exactly where traditional layering saturates, and (ii) full human review of AI-flagged alerts is not optimal: increasing analyst capacity toward 100% coverage cuts false alarms by roughly 20-fold but simultaneously lowers system-level detection probability, because imperfect analyst accuracy is then applied to every alert rather than a filtered subset. These results give the widely repeated qualitative recommendation of "balanced human-AI collaboration" a precise, testable form and suggest an interior-optimum capacity ratio as a concrete design target for security operations centers (SOCs), including those securing IT/OT-converged critical infrastructure.
2609.25921.paper_summary_zh: 網路安全文獻廣泛記錄了人工智慧（AI）在威脅檢測、事件回應和預防方面的操作效益，同時提出了關於過度自動化、演算法偏見和分析師技能侵蝕的質性擔憂。至今仍然缺乏一個正式的、可證偽的模型，將文獻中反覆出現的三個構念聯繫起來：深度防禦理論、人工智慧模式識別理論，以及人類與AI在安全操作中的合作。本文發展了這樣的模型。我們將分層防禦形式化為一個伯努利檢測級聯，其中AI增強在各層之間以乘法方式進入；我們將每一層的模式識別行為形式化為一個奈曼-皮爾森/貝葉斯檢測器，並導出閉合形式的最優閾值；我們將人類-AI 分診形式化為一個容量受限的級聯，並明確量化檢測概率與假警報（「警報疲勞」）率之間的權衡。一個在具體但現實的操作點進行的蒙地卡羅/分析模擬顯示：（i）AI增強在防禦層之間的複合效應，正好在傳統分層飽和的地方提供其最大的邊際收益，並且（ii）對AI標記警報的完全人類審查並不是最佳的：將分析師的能力提高至100%覆蓋率大約可以將假警報減少20倍，但同時降低系統層級的檢測概率，因為不完美的分析師準確性會應用於每一個警報，而不是過濾後的子集。這些結果為廣泛重複的「平衡人類-AI合作」的質性建議提供了一個精確、可測試的形式，並建議一個內部最佳的容量比率作為安全操作中心（SOCs）的具體設計目標，包括那些保護IT/OT融合的關鍵基礎設施的中心。
